en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Dyad on Accompanied by Vicāra (Savicāraduka).

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, accompanied by sustained thought (*savicāra*), there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive and is without sustained thought (*nasavicāra*), by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. [There are] six under root, three under object … pe … six under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, without sustained thought (*avicāra*), there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor reactive and is without sustained thought, by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, without sustained thought, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor reactive … [and so on].
A state that is non-surveying (*avicāra*) does not arise with a root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive (*anidassana-appaṭigha*) and non-surveying, there arise states that are neither demonstrable nor reactive and neither surveying, and states that are neither demonstrable nor reactive and non-surveying, with a root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root-cause, three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance, three.
